lessons.title: Indian Spices: Masalas and Curry Powders
lessons.body:
Indian cooking uses blends called masalas, not single 'curry powder'. A basic garam masala starts with whole spices: 4 tbsp coriander seeds, 2 tbsp cumin seeds, 1 tbsp black peppercorns, 1 tbsp green cardamom pods, 2 cinnamon sticks (2-inch), 1 tbsp cloves, and 1 tsp grated nutmeg. Dry-roast in a heavy pan over medium heat for 2-3 minutes until fragrant, cool, then grind in a spice grinder or mortar. Store in an airtight jar away from sunlight for up to 3 months.

For a simple everyday curry powder, mix: 3 tbsp coriander powder, 2 tbsp cumin powder, 1 tbsp turmeric powder, 1 tsp cayenne, 1 tsp black pepper, and 1 tsp fenugreek powder. This is enough for 4-6 pots of stew. Use 1-2 tsp per 500g of meat or vegetables.

In Africa, you can source whole spices from local markets: coriander and cumin are grown in Ethiopia, Sudan, and Morocco. Turmeric comes from Nigeria and Ghana. Cardamom is imported but available in Indian shops in Nairobi, Lagos, or Accra. Buy whole and grind fresh for best flavour.

To make a quick chicken curry for 4: heat 2 tbsp oil, add 1 chopped onion, fry until golden. Add 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and 2 tsp curry powder, stir 30 seconds. Add 500g chicken pieces, 2 chopped tomatoes, and 1 cup water. Simmer 20 minutes. Finish with 1 tsp garam masala and fresh coriander. Serve with rice or chapati.

Key tools: a dry frying pan, a spice grinder or clean coffee grinder, and airtight glass jars. Never use wet spoons in spice jarsâmoisture causes mould. Label with date. For deeper flavour, bloom ground spices in hot oil for 10-15 seconds before adding other ingredients. This releases fat-soluble aromas. Adjust heat by increasing or decreasing cayenne. For a smokier taste, add 1/2 tsp smoked paprika. Practice with small batches until you know your preferred ratios.

lessons.title: Thai Spices: Lemongrass, Galangal, and Kaffir Lime
lessons.body:
Thai cooking relies on fresh aromatics: lemongrass, galangal, and kaffir lime leaves. Lemongrass has a stiff stalk; use only the lower 10-15 cm. Bruise it with the back of a knife or a pestle to release oils. Galangal looks like ginger but is harder, pinker, and piney. Slice it thinâit stays woody. Kaffir lime leaves are glossy, double-lobed; tear them to release citrus aroma. These three form the base of tom yum and many curries.

For a simple Thai green curry paste (makes about 1 cup): blend 10 fresh green bird's eye chilies, 3 stalks lemongrass (sliced thin), 5 cm galangal (peeled and sliced), 6 kaffir lime leaves (torn), 4 cloves garlic, 2 shallots, 1 tsp shrimp paste (optional), 1 tsp coriander seeds (toasted), 1/2 tsp cumin seeds (toasted), 1 tsp white pepper, and 1 tsp salt. Pound in a mortar or pulse in a blender with 2 tbsp water. Store in a jar in the fridge for up to 2 weeks, or freeze in ice cube trays.

In Africa, lemongrass grows easily in warm, wet climatesâplant a stalk in a pot near a window. Galangal is harder to find but Asian markets in Johannesburg, Lagos, or Nairobi stock it frozen or fresh. Kaffir lime trees grow in tropical Africa; if you cannot find leaves, substitute 1 tsp lime zest plus a pinch of bay leaf, though flavour differs.

To make a quick Thai chicken curry for 4: heat 1 tbsp oil, fry 2 tbsp curry paste for 1 minute. Add 400ml coconut milk, 500g chicken thigh pieces, 1 cup water. Simmer 15 minutes. Add 1 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tsp sugar, and a handful of Thai basil. Serve with jasmine rice. For vegetarians, use tofu or mushrooms.

Tools: a granite mortar and pestle (best) or a small blender; a fine grater for galangal; a sharp knife. Buy lemongrass with firm, pale green stalksâavoid dry, brown ones. Store fresh lemongrass in the fridge for 2 weeks or freeze sliced. Kaffir lime leaves freeze well for 6 months. Always taste and adjust: Thai food balances sour (lime), salty (fish sauce), sweet (sugar), and spicy (chili).

lessons.title: Mexican Spices: Chili, Cumin, and Oregano
lessons.body:
Mexican spice blends are built on dried chilies, cumin, and Mexican oregano. Common dried chilies: ancho (mild, fruity), guajillo (medium, tangy), chipotle (smoky, hot), and arbol (very hot). Toast dried chilies in a dry pan for 30 seconds per side until they puffâdo not burn, or they turn bitter. Soak in hot water for 20 minutes, then blend into a paste. This paste is the base for adobo, mole, and chili con carne.

A basic taco seasoning for 500g meat: mix 2 tbsp chili powder (from ground ancho/guajillo), 1 tsp ground cumin, 1 tsp dried Mexican oregano, 1 tsp garlic powder, 1 tsp onion powder, 1/2 tsp smoked paprika, 1/2 tsp cayenne, 1 tsp salt, and 1/2 tsp black pepper. Add 2 tbsp tomato paste and 1/4 cup water. Simmer 10 minutes.

In Africa, dried chilies are widely available: Nigerian suya pepper (a blend of chili, ginger, and peanuts) is similar. Ethiopian berbere includes chili, fenugreek, and cardamomâuse it as a substitute for ancho in stews. Cumin is grown in Morocco and Ethiopia. Mexican oregano is different from Mediterranean oregano; if unavailable, use 1 tsp dried marjoram plus 1/2 tsp dried thyme.

To make a quick chili con carne for 4: brown 500g beef mince. Add 1 chopped onion, 2 cloves garlic, and 2 tbsp taco seasoning. Stir 1 minute. Add 1 can (400g) chopped tomatoes, 1 can (400g) kidney beans, and 1 cup water. Simmer 30 minutes. Taste and add salt or a pinch of sugar. Serve with rice, tortillas, or cornbread.

Tools: a cast-iron skillet for toasting chilies, a blender for paste, and airtight jars. Buy whole dried chiliesâthey last 6-12 months in a cool, dark place. Ground spices lose flavour in 3 months. For a smoky flavour without chipotle, add 1/2 tsp smoked paprika. For heat, add cayenne or arbol powder. Always wear gloves when handling hot chilies, and do not touch your eyes. Adjust heat by using milder chilies like ancho.

lessons.title: Middle Eastern Spices: Sumac, Za'atar, and Baharat
lessons.body:
Middle Eastern cooking uses sumac (tangy, lemony), za'atar (a blend), and baharat (a warm spice mix). Sumac berries are dried and ground; they add sourness without liquid. Buy deep red sumacâbrown means old. Za'atar blend: 2 tbsp dried thyme, 2 tbsp toasted sesame seeds, 1 tbsp sumac, and 1/2 tsp salt. Mix and store in a jar. Use as a dip with olive oil and bread, or sprinkle on chicken, salads, and flatbread.

Baharat (meaning 'spices') varies by region. A common blend: 1 tbsp black pepper, 1 tbsp cumin, 1 tbsp coriander, 1 tbsp cinnamon, 1 tsp cloves, 1 tsp cardamom, 1 tsp nutmeg, and 1 tsp paprika. Grind whole spices for best flavour. Use 1-2 tsp per 500g meat or vegetables. It is excellent in lamb stews, rice pilafs, and grilled meats.

In Africa, sumac grows wild in Morocco and Tunisia; you can buy ground sumac in North African markets. Za'atar thyme is similar to wild thyme in Ethiopia. Baharat spices are available in Ethiopian and Somali markets (berbere is a cousin). If you cannot find sumac, substitute 1 tsp lemon zest plus 1/2 tsp salt for each 1 tbsp sumac.

To make a quick chicken kebab for 4: mix 500g chicken cubes with 2 tbsp olive oil, 1 tbsp baharat, 1 tsp sumac, 2 cloves crushed garlic, and 1 tsp salt. Marinate 30 minutes. Thread on skewers and grill or pan-fry 10-12 minutes, turning. Serve with flatbread, sliced onion, and a sprinkle of za'atar.

Tools: a spice grinder, a small frying pan for toasting sesame seeds, and airtight jars. Toast sesame seeds for 2-3 minutes until goldenâthey burn quickly. Store za'atar in the fridge to keep sesame fresh. Sumac lasts 1 year in a cool, dark place. Baharat lasts 6 months. For a quick dip: mix 2 tbsp za'atar with 4 tbsp olive oil and 1 tbsp lemon juice. Serve with bread. Adjust salt and sumac to taste.

lessons.title: North African Spices: Harissa and Ras el Hanout
lessons.body:
North African cuisine features harissa (a chili paste) and ras el hanout (a complex spice blend). Harissa is from Tunisia; ras el hanout from Morocco. Harissa: soak 10 dried guajillo or ancho chilies in hot water 20 minutes. Blend with 4 cloves garlic, 1 tsp caraway seeds, 1 tsp coriander seeds, 1 tsp cumin seeds, 1 tsp salt, 2 tbsp olive oil, and 1 tbsp lemon juice. Store in a jar with a layer of oil on top; keeps 1 month in fridge. Use 1 tsp per dish for heat and depth.

Ras el hanout means 'head of the shop'âevery spice seller has a unique blend. A basic version: 2 tbsp cumin, 2 tbsp coriander, 1 tbsp cinnamon, 1 tbsp paprika, 1 tsp cardamom, 1 tsp cloves, 1 tsp nutmeg, 1 tsp allspice, 1 tsp ginger, 1 tsp black pepper, and 1 tsp turmeric. Toast whole spices, grind, and mix. Use 1-2 tsp per 500g meat or vegetables.

In Africa, harissa ingredients are easy: chilies grow across the continent. Caraway and coriander are grown in Morocco and Egypt. Ras el hanout spices are available in North African markets; you can also use Ethiopian berbere as a substitute, but it is hotter. For a milder blend, reduce cayenne or chili powder.

To make a quick lamb tagine for 4: brown 500g lamb cubes in 2 tbsp oil. Add 1 chopped onion, 2 cloves garlic, and 2 tsp ras el hanout. Stir 1 minute. Add 1 can (400g) chopped tomatoes, 1 cup water, 1 cup dried apricots, and 1 tsp harissa. Simmer 1 hour until lamb is tender. Serve with couscous.

Tools: a spice grinder, a blender for harissa, and airtight jars. Toast whole spices for 2-3 minutes until fragrant. Store ras el hanout in a cool, dark place for up to 6 months. Harissa can be frozen in ice cube trays. For a quick marinade: mix 1 tbsp harissa, 1 tbsp olive oil, 1 tsp ras el hanout, and 1 tsp lemon juice. Coat chicken or fish and grill. Adjust heat by adding more or less harissa.

lessons.title: Caribbean Spices: Allspice, Nutmeg, and Scotch Bonnet
lessons.body:
Caribbean cooking uses allspice (pimento), nutmeg, and scotch bonnet peppers. Allspice berries taste like cinnamon, cloves, and nutmeg combined. Buy whole berries and grind fresh. Nutmeg is best grated wholeâuse a fine grater. Scotch bonnet is a fiery chili with a fruity, floral flavour. Handle with gloves; remove seeds to reduce heat. These spices form the base of jerk seasoning.

Jerk seasoning for 1kg chicken: blend 2 tbsp allspice berries (ground), 1 tsp grated nutmeg, 2 scotch bonnet peppers (deseeded for mild), 4 spring onions, 4 cloves garlic, 2 tbsp fresh thyme, 1 tbsp brown sugar, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp lime juice, 1 tsp black pepper, and 1 tsp salt. Marinate chicken 4 hours or overnight. Grill or bake at 200Â°C for 30-40 minutes.

In Africa, allspice is grown in Jamaica but also in parts of West Africa. Nutmeg comes from Grenada and also Equatorial Guinea. Scotch bonnet is similar to African bird's eye chili; you can substitute habanero or any hot chili. For a milder jerk, use 1 scotch bonnet and remove seeds.

To make a quick Caribbean rice and peas for 4: cook 2 cups rice with 1 can (400ml) coconut milk, 1 cup water, 1 can (400g) kidney beans, 1 tsp allspice, 1/2 tsp grated nutmeg, 1 tsp thyme, and 1 scotch bonnet (whole, pierced). Simmer 20 minutes. Remove pepper before serving. Add salt to taste.

Tools: a spice grinder, a fine grater, gloves for chilies, and a blender for jerk paste. Store whole allspice and nutmeg in a cool, dark place for up to 2 years; ground spices last 6 months. Jerk paste freezes well in ice cube trays. For a quick rub: mix 1 tbsp ground allspice, 1 tsp nutmeg, 1 tsp cayenne, 1 tsp thyme, and 1 tsp salt. Rub on pork, chicken, or fish. Adjust heat by using less scotch bonnet. Always wash hands and tools after handling hot peppers.

quiz.q: What is the main difference between garam masala and curry powder?
options: A) Garam masala is a blend, curry powder is a single spice
B) Garam masala is added at the end, curry powder is cooked in
C) Garam masala contains no turmeric, curry powder does
D) Garam masala is only for meat, curry powder for vegetables
quiz.explanation: Garam masala typically omits turmeric, while curry powder includes it for colour.

quiz.q: Which spice is NOT part of a basic garam masala?
quiz.explanation: Turmeric is not used in traditional garam masala; it is used in curry powder.

quiz.q: How should you prepare lemongrass for cooking?
options: A) Use the whole stalk, chopped
C) Discard the stalk and use only leaves
D) Soak in water for 1 hour
quiz.explanation: Only the lower part is tender and flavourful; bruising releases oils.

quiz.q: What is a good substitute for kaffir lime leaves?
options: B) Lime zest plus a pinch of bay leaf
quiz.explanation: Lime zest and bay leaf approximate the citrus and herbal notes.

quiz.q: Which dried chili is mild and fruity?
quiz.explanation: Ancho chilies are mild with a fruity, raisin-like flavour.

quiz.q: What is a key step when using dried chilies?
options: A) Soak in cold water overnight
B) Toast in a dry pan until puffed
quiz.explanation: Toasting rehydrates and releases oils; over-toasting makes them bitter.

quiz.q: What does sumac add to a dish?
quiz.explanation: Sumac has a tangy, lemony sourness.

quiz.q: Which spice is NOT typically in za'atar?
quiz.explanation: Za'atar is thyme, sesame, sumac, and salt; cinnamon is not used.

quiz.q: What does 'ras el hanout' mean?
quiz.explanation: It translates to 'head of the shop', indicating the best blend.

quiz.q: How should harissa be stored?
options: A) In a jar with oil on top, in the fridge
quiz.explanation: A layer of oil prevents mould; refrigeration extends shelf life.

quiz.q: Which spice is a key ingredient in jerk seasoning?
quiz.explanation: Allspice is the signature spice in Jamaican jerk.

quiz.q: What is a safe way to handle scotch bonnet peppers?
options: A) Wear gloves and avoid touching eyes
B) Rinse with water after cutting
C) Use bare hands but wash immediately
quiz.explanation: Gloves prevent capsaicin from irritating skin and eyes.

quiz.q: Which spice blend is used in North African tagines?
quiz.explanation: Ras el hanout is the classic Moroccan blend for tagines.

quiz.q: What is the best way to store whole spices?
options: A) In a clear jar on a sunny shelf
B) In an airtight jar in a cool, dark place
quiz.explanation: Light, heat, and moisture degrade spices; cool, dark, airtight is best.

quiz.q: Which spice is NOT part of a basic Thai green curry paste?
quiz.explanation: Cinnamon is not used in Thai green curry paste.

quiz.q: What is a common substitute for Mexican oregano?
quiz.explanation: Marjoram and thyme approximate the flavour of Mexican oregano.

quiz.q: Which African spice blend is similar to Mexican chili powder?
quiz.explanation: Berbere contains chili, fenugreek, and cardamom, similar to chili powder.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of blooming ground spices in oil?
options: C) To make them last longer
quiz.explanation: Blooming in hot oil extracts and intensifies flavour.

quiz.q: Which tool is best for grinding whole spices?
options: B) A spice grinder or mortar and pestle
quiz.explanation: A spice grinder or mortar preserves oils and gives consistent grind.

quiz.q: How long does homemade harissa last in the fridge?
quiz.explanation: With oil on top, harissa keeps about 1 month refrigerated.

quiz.q: Which spice is a key ingredient in Caribbean rice and peas?
quiz.explanation: Allspice (pimento) is traditional in rice and peas.

quiz.q: What is a good substitute for scotch bonnet pepper?
quiz.explanation: Habanero has similar heat and fruity flavour.

quiz.q: Which spice is NOT typically in baharat?
quiz.explanation: Lemongrass is Thai, not Middle Eastern.

quiz.q: What is the main ingredient in za'atar?
quiz.explanation: Za'atar is primarily dried thyme with sesame and sumac.

quiz.q: How should you toast sesame seeds for za'atar?
options: A) In a dry pan for 2-3 minutes until golden
C) In the oven at 180Â°C for 10 minutes
quiz.explanation: Dry toasting brings out nuttiness; they burn quickly.

quiz.q: Which spice is a key ingredient in jerk marinade?
quiz.explanation: Nutmeg, along with allspice, is essential in jerk.

quiz.q: What is the best way to store fresh lemongrass?
options: A) In the fridge for 2 weeks or freeze sliced
C) In water on the counter
quiz.explanation: Refrigeration or freezing preserves flavour.

quiz.q: Which African country is a major producer of cumin?
quiz.explanation: Morocco and Ethiopia are known for cumin production.

quiz.q: What is a common substitute for sumac?
quiz.explanation: Lemon zest and salt mimic sumac's sour, salty tang.

quiz.q: How long can you store ground spices for best flavour?
quiz.explanation: Ground spices lose potency after about 3 months.
